analysis.title: Worst In 20 Years: Hedge Fund VIPs Crushed As Goldman Warns The Cyclicals They Fled To Are Next
key_insights: Goldman's hedge fund VIP basket lagged the S&P 500 by 14pp over six months, matching its worst relative stretch in 20 years (Dec '08 -13pp, May '22 -15pp). In June it was beating the market by 10pp.
US equity L/S funds are up 5% YTD through Nov 19 vs S&P +6% and equal-weight S&P +12%. The VIP basket is down 3% YTD.
VIP excess returns have a 0.9 correlation with GS AI, semis, optical, neocloud and memory baskets, so the hedge fund long book is effectively one AI trade.
Crowding is extreme: the median hedge fund holds 70% of its long book in its top 10 positions, and the GS Hedge Fund Crowding Index hit a record high in Q3.
Fundamental L/S net leverage fell to 42% (0th percentile over 5 years, lowest since Liberation Day). Gross is 205% (74th percentile) and total prime book gross is 316% (98th percentile).
On a beta-adjusted basis, fundamental L/S net leverage fell 9 points this week and over 22 points since early October to 48.2%, a five-year low.

In Q3 funds cut TMT and added Financials (+254bp), Consumer Discretionary (+237bp), Industrials (+190bp), Staples (+154bp) and Utilities (+120bp) vs the Russell 3000. The Info Tech underweight widened 619bp to a record -2,267bp.

Funds entered Q4 with 10-year-high tilts to Health Care, Financials, Consumer Discretionary, Utilities and Staples simultaneously. Momentum exposure is the lowest since early 2023 and funds rotated from Growth to Value.

GS's Miller draws a 4Q18 analogy: High-Beta Cyclicals are +12% YTD while broad US AI is negative YTD. In 4Q18 high-beta cyclicals fell 23% and underperformed SPX by 10pp, and the basket now trades at 15x forward earnings, a 40% premium to its 2018 trough multiple.
Other 2018 laggards look exposed: Lending Sensitive is flat QTD vs a 15% plunge in 4Q18. UK Consumption and EU Domestic Consumption are each +12% QTD vs falls of 28% and 16% in 4Q18.

Fast money is light and slow money is full. CTAs, vol control and HF net exposure are near the low end of their ranges, while US equity ETF inflows, PB gross leverage are heavy and mutual fund cash is at a record low. Large-cap growth mutual fund beta is 1.38 on a 3-month basis (90th percentile) vs the April 2022 high of 1.58.

Miller prefers the long High vs Low FCF pair, and Healthcare over Staples within defensives. A new 2027 Top US Healthcare Themes basket is proposed, but Health Care is already the largest HF net overweight at +960bp.
Miller likes China High Dividends (+3.4% since last week) and would fade relief rallies in the China Competition basket (11x forward earnings, a value trap).

GS pitches the Conditional Downvar Strategy as a tail hedge. After a 3.7% down move the S&P is inside the protection corridor, with the barrier about 2.5% below spot as of Friday morning. Under 5% of basket flows were buy-to-open.
Median S&P 500 stock short interest ranks in the 92nd percentile of 20 years, with Utilities (99th), Staples and Health Care (95th) most shorted.

sector_views.rationale: Miller prefers Healthcare over Staples and likes structural growth themes, though HFs are already +960bp net overweight.
Miller prefers Healthcare versus Staples within defensives. Staples are a crowded HF tilt and heavily shorted.

Brian Garrett's 2018-path scenario pencils in this S&P level.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Fed capitulation is not priced, and hawkishness is a risk for lending-sensitive stocks.

trade_ideas.description: Long GS High vs Low FCF pair basket (GSPUFCFP US, GSPEFCFP Europe)
trade_ideas.rationale: The desk's preferred long exposure given crowded cyclicals and AI.

trade_ideas.description: Long Healthcare vs Staples, via 2027 Top US Healthcare Themes basket (GSCBHC27)
trade_ideas.rationale: Structural growth themes with low correlation to oil, rates and AI, with multiples falling from 28x to 19x 2028E.
trade_ideas.risk: Health Care is already the largest HF net overweight at +960bp.

trade_ideas.description: GS Conditional Downvar Strategy (GSISCVS1) tail hedge on SPX, barrier about 2.5% below spot
trade_ideas.rationale: Convex payoff if the selloff accelerates, as in sudden deep selloffs like 2008 and 2020.
trade_ideas.risk: A reversal that exits the corridor can lock in delta hedge losses, and the strategy struggles in slow grinds like 2022.

trade_ideas.description: Long China High Dividends basket (GSXACHHN), fade rallies in China Competition basket (GSXECHNX)
trade_ideas.rationale: China Competition is cheap at 11x forward earnings only if consensus estimates are trusted, a value trap.

trade_ideas.description: Short High-Beta Cyclicals (GSXUHBCY), Lending Sensitive (GSXULEND), UK and EU consumption baskets on 4Q18 analog
trade_ideas.rationale: Hedge fund and real money crowding in cyclicals with high valuations, and these baskets fell sharply in 4Q18.
trade_ideas.risk: Growth optimism stays high and rotations continue out of AI rather than into outright equity downside.

risk_factors: Cyclical and defensive tilts are at record crowding, so forced selling could hit the rotation trades.
Real money (mutual funds with record-low cash, high beta) has not de-risked.
Fed hawkishness and tightening in the lending market could hit lending-sensitive names.
A squeeze from washed-out fast money is the counter-risk to bearish positioning.
The tail hedge can lose if the selloff reverses (as in 2018 corridor exit) or grinds slowly.
Growth uncertainty replacing inflation anxiety would hurt high-beta cyclicals.

tension_points.bull_case: Washed-out fast money (nets at five-year lows, AI cut, Momentum purged) means any spark could trigger a short-covering squeeze.
tension_points.bear_case: Funds rotated into record-crowded cyclical and defensive tilts, and real money with record-low cash and high beta has not sold. 2018 saw cyclicals crack rather than squeeze.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A reversal next week that takes the S&P out of the protection corridor, as in 2018, or a Fed capitulation, would undermine the bearish case for cyclicals only if credit and cyclicals hold.
